sections.h2: Which offices deal with property tax in Trimble County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Three offices in Bedford handle a Trimble County tax account. The Property Valuation Administrator sets the value, the sheriff collects the money, and the county clerk keeps the deeds and takes over any bill that goes delinquent. The county's own page says the PVA assesses all property at fair cash value under KRS 132.450 and builds the tax roll that every taxing district then uses.

Trimble County offices that touch a tax bill, from the county's published office pages

The sheriff's page lists tax collection beside law enforcement, vehicle inspections and court security, so call ahead if you need a payoff figure in writing for a closing.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Trimble County, and why does that matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Trimble is a small river county in north central Kentucky, formed in 1837 with Bedford as its seat. Its western edge is the Ohio River, facing Indiana, and a north to south ridge splits the land into two drainage areas. At about 152 square miles of land it is the fifth smallest Kentucky county by land area, and the 2020 census counted every resident as rural.

Milton, the largest town, sits where US 421 meets KY 36 across the river from Madison, Indiana. Bedford, at the crossing of US 421 and US 42, is the seat of government. The Trimble County Generating Station, a coal fired plant of LG&E and KU on 2,200 acres beside the Ohio about 50 miles northeast of Louisville, is the best known industrial site.

Census QuickFacts gives a picture of what a buyer will see in the county:

  • Population estimate for July 2025: 8,701, up 2.7 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Owner occupied homes: 79.7 percent.
  • Median value of an owner occupied home (2020 to 2024): $172,000.
  • Median household income: $66,027, with 12.5 percent of people in poverty.
  • Average commute: 27.2 minutes.
  • Persons 65 or older: 21.4 percent, the group the homestead exemption is written for.

Roughly 94 percent of residents had lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is low. A seller who arrives with a clean tax account and a deed that already meets the clerk's rules stands out from the rest of a thin market.

sections.h2: How much tax does a typical Trimble County house carry?
sections.html:
The state portion alone is easy to work out. For 2025 the Department of Revenue set the state real property rate at 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value, down from 10.9 cents in 2024. On a house at the county's $172,000 median that comes to $182.32 a year to the state.

County, school and special district levies are added on top, and the Trimble County sheriff or the PVA can tell you the total rate for a particular parcel. Ask for the rate that applies to the address, because districts differ from one end of the county to the other.

If the owner qualifies for the homestead exemption, the same house is taxed on $122,900 instead, and the state portion falls to about $130.27. Any early payment discount applies to the entire bill, not only the state share.

sections.h2: When are Trimble County tax bills due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Kentucky runs one statewide payment calendar under KRS 134.015, and the sheriff follows it. The sheriff works from that calendar every year.

  • Paid in full by November 1: 2 percent off the amount due.
  • November 2 through December 31: the printed amount, with no discount and no penalty.
  • January: a 5 percent penalty.
  • After January 31: a 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff's add on fee.

The sheriff keeps taking payments until the close of business on April 15. After that the unpaid bills go to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency and a lien is recorded on the parcel. Interest of 1 percent a month starts then, with clerk and county attorney fees on top.

As an illustration from the Department of Revenue, a $1,000 bill reaches the clerk at $1,254.00 and costs $1,387.79 if cleared within five business days. The figures use an assumed 4 percent sheriff commission, so Trimble County's real numbers can differ a little.

sections.h2: Can an unpaid Trimble County tax bill stop a sale?
sections.html:
It can complicate one. A delinquent tax lien follows the land for up to 11 years under KRS 134.420, whoever owns it, so a buyer's title company will want it cleared. The clerk holds the delinquent account after April 15 and takes payments until the annual sale, which comes at least 90 days after the transfer.

Before the sale, the county attorney mails a first notice within 30 days of the transfer and a second one that names the sale date. The clerk then advertises the list at least 30 days ahead. Pay from the sale proceeds at closing and get the clerk to confirm the account is released.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Trimble County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA. A conference with the PVA or a deputy is required before any appeal is accepted, and the PVA must explain how your value was reached at that meeting.

The tax roll is open for inspection for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May, and the PVA announces the dates in the county's largest newspaper. If the conference leaves you unsatisfied, file with the county clerk by the close of business on the day after the inspection period ends. The local board of assessment appeals then meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection closes.

  • Bring photos of defects, repair bids, insurance papers and recent nearby sales.
  • Evidence counts only if it is handed to the board with the PVA or a deputy present.
  • The board must explain in writing any change it makes, up or down.
  • You may record the hearing on audio.

Bills printed before the case ends use the value you claimed. If the final value is higher, a supplemental bill follows for the difference.

sections.h2: Who can claim the Kentucky homestead exemption in Trimble County?
sections.html:
Homeowners aged 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled by a federal agency or a retirement system, may apply. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the exemption is $49,100, subtracted from assessed value before rates are applied.

The application goes to the Trimble County PVA at the Bedford office. Age is proved with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. A disability claim has to be renewed every year unless the owner is a veteran with a service connected disability or has been found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What should a Trimble County seller settle before closing?
sections.html:
The tax account is the first item, and the deed is the second. A Kentucky deed has to give the full names and mailing addresses of both sides, state the full consideration, and name an in care of address for that year's tax bill, under KRS 382.135. The grantor's source of title must be cited under KRS 382.110, and the deed is recorded in the county where the land sits.

  • Ask the sheriff whether the current bill is paid and what the payoff is if not.
  • Check with the clerk for any certificate of delinquency recorded against the parcel.
  • Confirm with the PVA whether a homestead exemption is on file and whether the buyer will need to reapply.
  • Have the deed show the buyer's in care of address so the next bill finds its way to the new owner.

A seller with a back tax bill, an inherited house or a rental in poor condition can close with a cash buyer and let the payoff come out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Trimble County?
faqs.a: The Trimble County Sheriff collects it. The office is at 30 Hwy 42 E in Bedford, and the phone number is (502) 255-7138. The PVA only values the property and does not take payment.

faqs.q: Is the Trimble County discount still available?
faqs.a: Only before November 1 of each tax year. The 2 percent discount applies to bills paid in full by that date, and the printed amount is due from November 2 through December 31. Penalties start in January.

faqs.q: Where do I file an assessment appeal in Trimble County?
faqs.a: You file it with the county clerk after a conference with the PVA. The deadline is the close of business on the day after the 13 day inspection period ends, which starts on the first Monday in May.

faqs.q: How much is the Kentucky homestead exemption for a Trimble County owner?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It applies to owners 65 or older and to totally disabled owners, and it is claimed at the PVA in Bedford.

faqs.q: What happens to a Trimble County bill that stays unpaid after April 15?
faqs.a: It moves to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency, a lien is recorded, and interest of 1 percent a month plus clerk and attorney fees accrue. The clerk can sell the certificate to a third party at the annual sale.
